summary:
Feasible for stage boundaries, not for iterations inside a loop.

What it is. An optional `stop_at` record in state.md, set by a new verb `shiploop stop-at --set after:<stage>`. The transition that accepts that stage and moves past it is saved already paused, through the existing pause. The model then gets a short packet (1,139 characters in my prototype) that says end your turn. Nothing is killed, so metrics.json, result.json and the Run Review export get written. `resume` continues the run in place.

How a model-started run gets it. The harness arms it with the verb as soon as state.md appears. The model's first accept comes 7 to 16 s later on six Claude hello runs and 81 to 304 s later on Grok and Luna battleship runs (recomputed from timeline.json). An environment variable also reaches Claude, Grok and Codex, but it is ambient and cannot arm a continuation, so I do not recommend it. Seeded and resumed runs arm synchronously.

What the two attacks changed. A stop into static-checks or verify silently dropped the lint pass (reproduced; a one-line fix is verified). The held packet contradicted the status block and SKILL.md. Arming had gaps for inner stages and re-arming. No test pinned that a stopped run is not relaunched. All accepted.

What it cannot do. Stop at pass N of an Improve or Backchain loop: the runtime is hash pinned and S-10 forbids a cap. Test changed engine code on a stored real plan: a continuation runs the planning-time install.

Unmeasured: how reliably models end their turn on the final packet text in long runs, minutes saved, and the arming margin under load.

Build first: the SPEC S-16 commit, then the engine core (about 150 lines with tests), then the harness, then three live rungs: a Claude hello stop at after:intake, a seeded Grok stop at after:test-spec, and the Grok planning-only probe.
option:
NAME. Stop point. State key `stop_at`, verb `stop-at`, harness flag `--stop-at`. Printed text says 'paused at the requested stop point' because 'stopped' is the Until Loop terminal status and the host Stop hook's word.

WHY A SCRIPT PAUSE AND NOT A HARNESS MARKER. A script-written marker plus a harness kill still needs the arming channel and the kill, and leaves the model inside the next action. A poll cannot be deterministic: baseline, test-author and test-red are often 0 to 12 s windows [M, report 2], and the 'stage baseline' poll lost a baseline accepted 32 s after test-spec [M, report 4]. Only a pause saved inside the accepting transition stops cleanly.

GRAMMAR v1: `after:<stage>`, one of 33 stages (shiploop_stage_spec _ROWS has 34: 7 prelude, 18 inner, 9 outer [M, ran it]; `handoff` is refused because it ends the run). Later forms, increment I8 only if the probes need them: `review:<stage>`, `before:<stage>`, `#n`. The grammar line is a constant STOP_AT_FORMS pinned equal to the SPEC text.

MEANING of after:S. It fires once, on the first transition after arming that (a) adds a history row for S with outcome done, including a row the script itself records as not applicable (shiploop_navigator._record_not_applicable_tests writes done rows in the same transition: five forms, after:step-plan, test-spec, baseline, test-author and test-red, all pause at the same revision with the cursor on implement for a docs-only item [M, re-ran lensC]); (b) leaves S, that is current_stage(after) != S, so with inline delegation after:implement fires after the last planned step and never after step 1 [M, _apply_result: implement_progress keeps the cursor on implement]; (c) leaves the run active. It never fires on blocked, revise, repeat, replan, an exact replay, or improve-reconcile. For an Improve-reviewed stage it fires at the improve-complete import (finish_improve), never at the producer's complete, which only parks the action [M, re-ran lensB: producer replay and import replay leave state.md unchanged, resume keeps the same action id]. This is the 'first test-spec accept' the planning-only probes need. The reason text says so when S was recorded not applicable.

STATE KEY (optional, like delegation_hold): `stop_at: {when: 'after:<stage>', reached: null | {revision: <int>, action: <history row action id>}}`. Added to _STATE_KEYS and the optional set in _validate_current_state with shape validation. No source or reason field: how it was given is the harness's record. HELD is derived, never stored: status is paused and reached.revision equals the state revision. A later pause by a person has another revision and renders as an ordinary pause. After resume the record stays as audit and is inert. The one definition of held lives in the engine and is exposed to the harness through two new hook-status JSON fields, `stop_at` and `stop_held` (hook-status is read-only and lock-free [M, shiploop_protocol.hook_status]), so the harness never re-derives it (S-12).

FIRING. `_stop_check(before, after)` wraps `_apply_result` (core renamed, wrapper added), the one choke point of apply and finish_improve and so of complete, improve-complete, the dry run and the harness seed script [M]. It calls `control(after, 'pause', reason)` (one pause implementation; the reason avoids the _HOUSEKEEPING_PAUSE words [M, regex read]) and sets reached to the paused revision. Accept and pause are two revisions in one save [M, lab_stop_proto.out]. The save then runs the same side effects as any transition. Dispatch order is apply, completion_guard, _lint_transition, save, _lint_finish, _item_commit, _knowledge_close, emit [M, dispatch read]. FIX FOUND BY ATTACK 1 (reproduced [M, lensA_lint.py]): lint.on_transition returns before the advisory-lint and report-lint pass when after.status is not active, so a stop that lands on static-checks (after:skill-validate) or verify (after:static-checks) silently dropped the lint record: armed run wrote only lint/<action>-inventory.md while the unarmed twin also wrote lint/<action>.md, and nothing reran it after resume. The other entry writes (lint item base, test-loop contract, quality contract, change inventory) do not key on status and are unaffected [M, lensD]. The fix is one line: lint_view reports a held stop as active (the transition's own hooks run as if it were active; its only consumer of the view status is on_transition [M, grep]). Verified in a scratch copy: the armed run then writes both lint files, state still paused at revision 27 [M, finalA_lint.py]. The attacker's alternative, applying the stop in dispatch after _lint_transition, is rejected: it stops pure apply, the dry run and the seed script from firing and splits the choke point.

VERB. `shiploop stop-at --run-dir R --set after:<stage>` | `--clear` | `--check SPEC`. `--check` is grammar and stage validation only, needs no run and no --run-dir (handled in main before the run lookup, like hook-status); it is the harness's preflight, so an old install (no verb, rc 2) or a typo is refused before any host cost. --set and --clear need an existing run, take the run lock, bump the revision like set_lint_mode, print one line ('Stop point armed: after:test-spec (revision N)'), and leave the pending action untouched [M, report 1 e6: the model's complete was accepted after arming].

IDEMPOTENCE (accepted from attack 1): --set with a record equal to the whole stored record {when: X, reached: null} is a no-op. A consumed record (reached not null) with the same `when` is replaced by a fresh one, so 'stop after implement of each item' is arm, fire, resume, re-arm.

ARMING REFUSALS (rule corrected by both attacks; one implementation, the engine's _accepted_done that already draws the status marks): refused for a terminal run; a held run, for --set and --clear (resume first); an unknown stage; `handoff`; bad grammar; a prelude or outer stage S with (None, S) in _accepted_done; an inner stage S with (cursor work item, S) in _accepted_done; an inner stage while the cursor is in the outer phase. _accepted_done follows revise and reconcile [M, ran it: after a revise at implement the item's step-plan..test-red keys are gone and only select-work remains], so after:test-spec is armable again after a revise and after:spec after a reconcile. A stop for the next work item's stage is armed in two steps at the boundary before it (for example arm after:carry-forward, resume, then arm after:test-spec); a `#n` form is I8. 'Already accepted' errors name the revision and the item.

VALIDATION AND RETRY GUARD. No init or workspace-start flag, so there is no retry guard to write (flags were dropped as KISS; if ever added, the guard is a copy of _require_retry_backchain_passes).

OLD RUNS. A run saved without the key loads and means no stop (absence is the defined value, not a migration). A run saved with it is refused by an older ShipLoop as 'unexpected: stop_at' [M, _validate_current_state]. A required key (the lint and backchain_passes precedent) would refuse every saved run at the next release, including in-flight E2E runs. Owner decision 2.

WHEN THE POINT DOES NOT OCCUR. The record keeps reached null and the run goes on to done. `status` appends 'Stop point after:X was never reached' (status_block itself is untouched except the held branch below, so active packets stay byte-identical, S-7, and the model never sees an armed stop until it fires). The harness fails its `stop` verdict as not honoured, never a pass.

NOT AN S-10 CAP. The stage form fires after the stage's own loop has ended on its condition. It never interrupts, counts or ends a loop. It is a requested pause, like the user's pause, which S-10 already lists as a way a loop ends.

stop_kinds.meaning: Pause when the stage is accepted done and the cursor has left it. First occurrence after arming; for an Improve-reviewed stage this is after its review import.
stop_kinds.mechanism: shiploop_navigator: _stop_check wrapping _apply_result (called by apply and finish_improve): new history rows with outcome done for S, current_stage(after) != S, status active, then control pause and reached revision. lint_view treats a held stop as active so the transition hooks are unchanged. Verified [M]: 33 after: forms fire once at the right cursor (report 1 e9_stage_matrix.py, 33 of 41 forms); five forms on a not-applicable item (re-ran lensC); a real vendored Improve child, producer replay and import replay unchanged, resume continues (re-ran lensB); lint parity on the stage that arrives at static-checks (re-ran lensA, then finalA with the fix).
stop_kinds.packet_text:
ShipLoop navigator | <next stage> | revision <N> | STOP POINT REACHED
The run stopped on purpose at the requested stop point after:<stage>: the owner asked for a pause here to test or measure. Nothing failed and no question is open.
End your turn now with one line saying so. Run no ShipLoop command and start no other work: the owner resumes this run.
If your context was lost, this is the whole state; reprinting it changes nothing: <next command>

<status block with a held branch: 'Stopped: paused at the requested stop point after:<stage>; the owner resumes the run.'>
(not-applicable case adds: <stage> was recorded not applicable for this item.)
No callback, no resume command, no keepalive marker. Measured 1,139 characters with a 190-character scratch path in the recovery line [M, held_packet_len.py]; the draft's 'about 700' was wrong. The generic paused packet is 11,064 to 18,874 characters and is cut at PRINT_LIMIT 16,000 [M, reports 1 to 4; re-seen in lab_paused.out].
stop_kinds.value: High, and the smallest useful slice. Planning-only probes (after:test-spec) and 'stop after stage X' become deterministic with no kill, so metrics.json, result.json and the export are written. Removes the miss seen this week (the 'stage baseline' poll lost a baseline accepted 32 s after test-spec [M, report 4]). Three runs this week have no metrics.json, result.json or review-export because their host was killed [M, re-listed: v1200-battleship-luna, v1210-battleship-grok-medium, v1210-battleship-luna-xhigh].

stop_kinds.meaning: Pause on arrival at the stage, before its action is worked.
stop_kinds.mechanism: Same _stop_check hook with an arrival condition (cursor changed to S, status active). For a first arrival it equals after:<predecessor>. It differs when the predecessor is skipped as not applicable (before:test-spec never arrives for such an item) and on a revise re-entry (before:step-plan fires again). [I: reasoned from _apply_result, not prototyped.]
stop_kinds.packet_text: Same shape: 'stopped on purpose at the requested stop point before:<stage>; <stage> has not started'.
stop_kinds.value: Medium to low. Only the revise re-entry is new. Defer to I8.

stop_kinds.meaning: Pause when the producer result of an Improve-reviewed stage is parked and no review has started: after the Backchain planning child when the stage is plan, before the Improve review of spec, step-plan, test-spec and so on.
stop_kinds.mechanism: shiploop_navigator.apply, the park branch that sets active_improve, after the revision bump. Valid for the 7 always-reviewed stages plus carry-forward (last item only). Prototyped: 8 review: forms fire once [M, report 1 e9]; resume keeps the same child parked [M, report 1 e2/e3]. Never fires for an item the script records as not applicable [M, report 3 prototype_na.py].
stop_kinds.packet_text: Same shape: 'the stage result is accepted for review and no review has started'.
stop_kinds.value: Medium. With after:test-strategy it brackets the host-written Backchain plan loop (before it, and after it but before the plan review), the nearest script-owned answer to 'Backchain pass N'. Defer to I8.

stop_kinds.meaning: Pause after review pass N of an Improve child, before pass N+1.
stop_kinds.mechanism: None without touching the vendored Until Loop. The pass counter (action_number) advances only when the model runs the runtime's done; ShipLoop sees the child at its start, its terminal packet and the optional improve-commit [M, report 1 e2: state.md stays at revision 5 across a pass]. The runtime is hash pinned (skills/improve/runtime/until-loop/PROVENANCE.json, asserted by test/improve.test.sh [M, report 1]) and a requested pass count inside its contract would read as a cap under S-10. Partial routes: (1) the harness polls the receipt, runs the existing pause, then kills the host [M, report 1 e8]: nondeterministic and today's kill pain; (2) gate improve-commit at pass >= N [I, not prototyped]: only passes that changed files reach it.
stop_kinds.packet_text: Not applicable for the script. A harness-assisted pause uses the generic paused packet, which is cut at the print limit (risk 13).
stop_kinds.value: Unknown. Pass counts, change flags and minutes are already measurable after the fact from the receipts (Luna xhigh: 22 passes in 5 children, Grok medium 26 passes in 5 children [M, stage-clock.md]). Recommend not building. Revisit only if a measurement needs a pause mid-loop, as a separate owner decision about the vendored runtime.

stop_kinds.meaning: Pause after pass N of the Backchain planning child at plan.
stop_kinds.mechanism: The Backchain loop contract is written by the host model (SPEC S-10 carve-out). ShipLoop keeps no pass counter, only the backchain_passes option, and never sees the passes.
stop_kinds.packet_text: Not applicable. Use after:test-strategy (before the loop) and review:plan (after the loop, before the plan review) to bracket it.
stop_kinds.value: None as a pass stop. The bracketing pair covers the useful cases (plan once, then test the review or later stages).

stop_kinds.meaning: Pause when the state revision counter reaches N.
stop_kinds.mechanism: Trivial in _stop_check, but the revision increments on every verb including arming and the pause itself, and differs run to run. [I: not prototyped.]
stop_kinds.value: Low. Not recommended: not deterministic across runs, so it would not make probes comparable. Skip.

how_a_model_started_run_receives_it:
THE CRUX. The model runs `workspace start` or `init` itself from the case prompt, so the harness cannot add a flag [M, events of v1210-battleship-grok-medium, v1210-battleship-luna-xhigh, v1190-hello-sonnet via report 4]. Candidates:

1. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE read at creation. Reaches the tool shell on all three hosts through the harness's own adapters [M, re-read: p3-env-claude-2, p3-env-grok and p3-env-codex events each show SHIPLOOP_STOP_AT=probe-value and a *_KEY-named variable]. End to end with a prototype engine the model ran init itself and the run paused with the model ending its turn on every host: Claude after:intake 5 turns, $0.159, 16.0 s; after:discovery 8 turns, $0.213, 30.0 s; after:research 10 turns, $0.251, 46.3 s; Grok after:intake 5 turns, $0.061; Codex after:intake 10 turns [M, re-read result events of p5-*]. That packet printed an owner-only resume command; the recommended packet does not, so this is evidence for the route, not for the final text. Costs: (a) first graph-affecting environment input (today SHIPLOOP_KEEPALIVE, _PROGRESS, _GIT_TIMEOUT are operational) and SKILL.md says environment settings do not change the ShipLoop versus launcher boundary [M, report 2]; (b) ambient: an exported variable silently pauses an unrelated production run, an S-14 stall hazard; (c) a second way to arm (S-12); (d) cannot arm a continuation (init is not rerun), so the verb is needed anyway; (e) Claude 2.1.289 CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB could scrub it [M, report 2, binary strings]; (f) a model-run `env` is denied by the Claude and Grok auto-mode classifiers [M, report 2], so the harness learns it worked only from state.md. Verdict: viable second choice, not built.
2. FILE IN THE WORK DIRECTORY read by init. Rejected [M]: launch() refuses a non-empty work directory ('working directory is not empty') and workspace start treats a non-empty one differently; a file beside the repository is an invisible ambient convention.
3. TEXT IN THE CASE PROMPT telling the model to pass a flag. Rejected: the model can omit or mistype it, it changes the request under test and the recorded prompt (init retries compare the prompt), and it is model-written glue (S-4, S-13).
4. HARNESS PRE-WRITES OR STARTS THE RUN (the --seed-at pattern). Right for seeded runs, wrong for planning-only probes: the model's own start is not exercised. Kept as the synchronous arm path: seed_run returns the run_dir before any host starts, so `--seed-at step-plan --stop-at after:test-spec` arms with no race and no state.md discovery [M, run.py seed_run]. SEED_STAGES is ('step-plan',) and the prelude rows are synthetic done rows, so prelude forms are refused on a seeded run by the arming rule. Seeding does not exercise the crux; model-started smokes stay in the ladder.
5. VERB AFTER INIT, run by the harness. RECOMMENDED. Host-independent (no environment or model dependence); one mechanism (S-12) that also serves continuation and a person at a terminal; validated against the live cursor; a late arming is refused by the script. Arming latency 0.22 to 0.27 s on a model-started workspace run [M, report 1 e6]. The race is state creation to the model's first accept, recomputed this pass from timeline.json under /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs [M]: Claude hello 7, 8, 9, 9, 11, 16 s (n=6; seat-reservations 14 s), Grok battleship 81 s, Luna xhigh 147 s, Luna 247, 272, 304 s. Stamps are whole seconds, so each is about plus or minus 1 s.

CADENCE (accepted from attack 2): one polling loop, not two. launch() keeps its single poll loop; `stop_when` generalises to a tick callable that returns None or a status label, and the poll period is 0.5 s while an arming is pending and 2 s otherwise. Margin on the shortest recorded first accept: 7 s minus about 0.5 s poll and 0.3 s verb, so about 6 s, or about 5 s allowing the stamp rounding. Under fanout load unmeasured. after:intake on a fast host is the only tight case; it is covered by a live per-host smoke that records the armed seconds and revisions, so the margin is measured, not asserted.

MECHANICS. Find state.md the way grade_shiploop does but only under out/.shiploop-runs and out/work, not rglob over home/ and build/ [M, grade_shiploop skips home and build]. Run `<installed cli> stop-at --run-dir R --set SPEC` (cli from host.plugin_cli, which the harness already uses [M]) with the host environment plus SHIPLOOP_KEEPALIVE=off (main() calls shiploop_keepalive.ensure_hooks for non-dry-run verbs [M, reports 2 and 3]). Run it in a thread because the verb waits on the run lock while a complete runs tests. Retry each tick on 'no run yet'; stop on rc 0, on a script refusal, or once the first accept is seen in timeline.json.

HONEST RECORDING (a stop that never took effect reads as not honoured, never a pass). Merged records (attack 2 KISS, accepted): (i) invocation.json `stop_point`: requested spec, route ('stop-at verb armed by the harness; synchronous for seeded and resumed runs'), preflight result of `stop-at --check SPEC`. (ii) stop-point.json, written atomically as each event occurs so it survives a killed harness: armed {run_dir, rc, stdout and stderr head, seconds after launch, revision before and after, tries}, reached {seconds, revision, row action}, host_ended {by: itself | grace | not-armed, seconds after reached}, released {by: null | harness | other, revision}. (iii) result.json `stop_point`: a copy plus recorded (the record read back from hook-status of the ARMED run_dir, not from grade_shiploop's choice, which picks the first done run else runs[0] [M]), held_at_end (hook-status `stop_held`), honoured and, when false, the reason. If grade_shiploop sees more than one run the `stop` reason says so. honoured is true only if arming rc was 0, recorded.when equals requested, reached is not null, and the stop was held at the end or released by the harness. The model's word is never evidence (S-9): reached comes from the history row the script wrote. A model that armed its own stop shows as a read-back mismatch; a model that resumed or halted shows as released by other and fails `stop`. A host ended by the grace backstop makes the `stop` verdict read 'honoured, host ignored the stop, ended after N s' and the batch summary line says so, so a model that ignored the packet is never a clean pass.
resume:
WHAT CLEARS A STOP. The existing `resume` verb [M, shiploop_navigator.control]: paused to active, same pending action id, status_reason popped, revision bumped; the next complete is accepted and does not fire again [M, re-ran lensB]. `stop_at.reached` stays as audit and is inert. To stop again: `stop-at --set` replaces a consumed record (order: resume, then --set, then continue). `--clear` removes a record and is refused while held. After a resume the continued session starts with `next`, which prints the active packet and its keepalive marker, so the host binds again. The keepalive Stop hook already lets a turn end on a paused run and drops the binding [M, shiploop_keepalive._decide: status not active gives decision allow], which is why the pause works with the hooks installed.

WHO RESUMES. The owner or the harness, never the model. The held packet prints no resume command; SKILL.md step 5 gets one sentence making a stop-point packet an end-your-turn packet (today it says paused or blocked packets 'use its printed resume command once' [M, SKILL.md]); status_block's held branch drops 'The packet prints the resume command' [M, status_block read; the unfixed line rendered on a held state]. A model that resumes anyway is detected, not prevented (honest-model guard, like --answer): the harness records released by other and fails `stop`. No `resume --release` flag: the model could type it too.

REFUSALS ON A HELD RUN. complete, improve-bind, improve-start, improve-commit, improve-complete and improve-reconcile raise StopPointHeld (a NavigatorError subclass raised at the top of dispatch) with its own footer, 'The run is stopped at a requested stop point: end your turn; do not retry', in place of the generic 'The run is still active: fix the result and resubmit in this turn; do not end the turn over a refused callback', which today contradicts an end-your-turn stop [M, shiploop_protocol.main; reproduced on a held scratch run]. halt stays available to a person; pause is refused by control as for any paused run.

SCRIPT-STOPPED RUN IN THE HARNESS (edits owned by the E2E session). run.py relaunches a host only while the status is active or None (the while loop in main; a paused run breaks with resume_stop 'ShipLoop run is paused') [M, re-read]. So after the stop fires a Grok or Codex host that ends its turn is not relaunched and main falls through to metrics.collect, result.json and review_export; Claude is not resumable at all (ClaudeHost has no resumable attribute; GrokHost and CodexHost set it [M, hosts.py]). The harness never kills first. Backstop: when the stop is reached and the host is still alive after a grace period (suggest 120 s, owner decision 5) the harness ends the process group; state is already durable, so no race, and no relaunch follows because the engine is paused. launch() returns the single label 'interrupted' for every stop_when and main treats it as the chain interrupt (writes interrupt.json, relaunches) [M], so a distinct label 'stopped' (reason grace or not-armed) is required and the chain branch keys on its own label.
- GRADE: a planned stop is graded on invoked, plugin and a new `stop` verdict. `process` passes for a host that exited by itself and reads 'n/a: ended by the harness after the stop (grace)' when the backstop ended it. `shiploop`, `committed` and `checks` read 'n/a: stopped at <point>' with a reason (pass None, left out of the all() list, the idiom regraded process and budget_facts(interrupted=True) already use) because grade_shiploop passes only for done plus report.html and committed_facts needs HEAD moved [M, lab_paused.out]. result.pass carries scope 'partial: stopped after <stage>'. No baseline row is written (as for seeded and resumed runs). A requested stop that was refused, never armed, never reached, or released by other fails `stop`; a refused or late arming ends the host at once (label stopped, reason not-armed) rather than spend a full run on a probe that cannot answer its question.
- TERMINATION RECORD: termination_facts and stopped_line say 'stopped at the requested stop point after <stage> (revision N)', not 'engine paused with <stage> never accepted' [M, lab_paused.out printed the wrong wording]. metrics.pending_stage needs an exemption for a held stop (the harness passes the engine's stop_held from hook-status into the engine dict metrics reads); without it collect() adds a phantom {stage: step-plan, outcome: null, incomplete: true} row [M, lab_export.out].
- EXPORT: no exporter change. RUN_STATUS maps paused and export_run succeeded on a real paused run ('paused after 0 min') [M, lab_export.out]. A facts line 'Stop point: after test-spec reached at revision N' is optional and belongs to the Run Review session. A stop before any accepted action skips the export ('missing results'); after:intake already has one.
- --RESUME-RUN of a HELD stop: today a paused run raises 'needs an active, blocked or finished ShipLoop run' [M, run.py main]. Proposed: a held stop (stop_held from hook-status) is a regrade like blocked, no host starts and metrics.json and result.json are refreshed, which also repairs a harness that was killed while the run was held. A user-paused or halted run is still refused (S-14). CONTINUATION IS MANUAL in v1 (attack 2, accepted: no --release-stop and no `--stop-at NEXT` release flow): the owner runs `shiploop resume --run-dir R` with the run's own CLI, then `run.py --resume-run X` continues the now-active run in place by the existing code path; `--stop-at NEXT` on --resume-run arms synchronously before the host launches, the same call used for --seed-at. Constraints that stay [M, run.py main]: a resumed run keeps the plugin it started on (reinstalling would replace that version's files and a bound Improve child records paths inside them), the version gate applies, and a Codex run cannot continue after a release because Codex replaces the plugin at session start.
- GOAL 2, honestly (attack 2, accepted): 'test later stages without paying for planning again' is served only for host, model and effort variation on the same plugin install. It is NOT served for testing a changed ShipLoop on a stored real plan: a continuation runs the planning-time install [M], and the released-fix cannot reach it. --continue-from cannot be used after a stop: it copies only <prior>/work and drops .git/worktrees and the run directory [M, run.py continue_from]. A relocated copy of a stopped output keeps absolute paths in state.md, workspace.md, context-index.md and the worktree .git link [M, probe_relocate*.py]; whether a later stage that writes the worktree then fails is inferred, not tested. An in-place snapshot and restore of the whole output directory worked (revision 5 restored to 3, trial reached 4 [M, probe_restore_in_place.py]; real snapshots about 100 to 250 MB [M, report 4]) but runs the same install. For changed-engine tests on later stages the existing cheap route is --seed-at (synthetic planning), and a relocatable snapshot is a separate design. Owner decision 7 asks which goal 2 means.

harness_changes.what: Engine core: stop_at key and validation, pure API, firing hook, held packet, status lines, lint-view fix, arming rule

spec:
A clause and harness rules are needed, in their own commit before any engine code, with the owner's dated decision. No relaxation of S-9 or S-10 is needed, because the stage forms fire only after a stage's loop has ended and ask nobody anything. Two things do need the owner: an explicit exception to S-6's callback and recovery command for the held packet, and the change to 'verdicts must all pass' for runs that stop on purpose. S-14 holds because the stop is opt-in and a held run waits like a user pause.

Anchor: S-1, S-6, S-9, S-14. Evidence: three runs this week have no metrics.json, result.json or review-export because the host was killed (v1200-battleship-luna, v1210-battleship-grok-medium, v1210-battleship-luna-xhigh [M, re-listed]); the 'stage baseline' poll lost a baseline accepted 32 s after test-spec [M, report 4]; Grok medium and Luna xhigh planning windows are 72.7 and 375.0 minutes [M, stage-clock.md].

EXACT TEXT.

(1) Append to S-10, after 'a user stop.': 'A requested stop point (S-16) is a user stop in this sense: it fires only after a stage's own loop has ended on its condition, ends no loop, counts nothing, and is never an iteration cap.'

(2) New design clause after S-15: '**S-16 A requested stop is the script's, never a kill.** The owner, or a harness acting for the owner, may record one stop point in a run's state (`stop_at`, set by the `stop-at` verb). It names a stage. The transition that accepts that stage and moves the cursor past it is saved already paused (status paused, the point named in the reason). The transition's own records and commits (the item and knowledge commits, the lint and test-loop entry records) are made as for any transition, then the script prints a short packet that tells the model to end its turn. That packet carries no callback and no resume command, and for it `next`, which reprints it, is the recovery command: this is the one exception to S-6's callback and recovery command. Only the owner resumes the run, with `resume`, and it continues in place. The model never sets, clears or releases a stop point. A stop point is a boundary the script itself crosses (a stage accepted), never an iteration count, an exit condition or a blocker: it ends no loop, skips nothing and asks nobody a question, so S-9 and S-10 hold unchanged. It is opt-in like `--delegation`: a run nobody armed never pauses, and an armed run waits for its owner as a user pause does (S-14 governs the runs nobody armed). Arming is refused when the script can prove the stage is already accepted for the run's current position; a point the run ends without reaching stays recorded as not reached and is never reported as a pass. A pass inside a loop that the Until Loop runtime counts is not a stop point until that runtime can honour one (owner decision to be recorded). (owner decision, <date the owner approves>; anchor: S-1, S-6, S-9, S-14 and the three killed runs named in the commit message)'

(3) In 'How the harness checks the clauses', add a row: '| S-16 | result.json `stop_point`: requested point, how it was given (route, exit code, output, seconds, revision, the armed run), recorded (read back from the engine through hook-status), reached or not reached, held at the end, who released it, how the host ended; stop-point.json holds the same as events occurred |'

(4) Replace the sentence 'Verdicts (invoked, plugin, process, shiploop, committed, checks) must all pass.' with: 'Verdicts (invoked, plugin, process, shiploop, committed, checks) must all pass, except on a planned stop (see Rules for the harness itself), where `shiploop`, `committed` and `checks` read n/a, `process` reads n/a when the harness ended the host after the stop, and `stop` is a verdict.'

(5) Add to 'Rules for the harness itself': '- **Planned stops.** `run.py --stop-at POINT` asks for a run that stops on purpose. The harness validates the point with the installed ShipLoop before any host starts, arms it through ShipLoop's `stop-at` verb as soon as the run's state exists (at once, for a seeded or resumed run), records how it was given (the verb's exit code and output, the time, the revision, the run armed) and whether it took effect (the engine's own read-back: reached or not reached), and never ends the host before the stop is saved. Such a run is graded on `invoked`, `plugin` and `stop` (recorded as asked, reached at the named boundary, and still held, or released by the harness, when the host ended). `shiploop`, `committed` and `checks` read 'n/a: stopped at <point>', never a pass; no baseline row is written; the run is evidence about the stages it ran and nothing after. A requested stop that was refused, never armed, never reached or released by anything but the harness fails `stop` and reads 'not honoured'. A host that does not end its turn within the grace period is ended by the harness after the stop is saved, and the verdict says so. metrics.json, result.json and the Run Review export are written as for any run. `--resume-run` of a held stop regrades it; the owner resumes the run with ShipLoop's `resume` before continuing it.'

(6) Pin tests, like the S-10 option pin: the grammar line in S-16 equals the engine's STOP_AT_FORMS constant, and SKILL.md names the stop-point exception.

risks:
Adversarial evaluation (SPEC Change admission), with dispositions after two attacks.

1. SILENT MISS: a late arming, a stage the run never reaches, or a not-applicable stage, so the run proceeds to full cost. Mitigated: the verb refuses a stage the engine's own _accepted_done shows accepted for the cursor's position (prelude, outer and inner) and an inner stage once the cursor is in the outer phase; a not-applicable row counts (test I2-3); a never-reached point stays reached null, `status` says so and the harness fails `stop` as not honoured (test I5-f); a refused arming ends the host at once. Accepted: a stage in the future cannot be proven absent (replan, carry-forward and reconcile can add or rewind work), so a future-stage point may still go unreached; the claim 'never silently missed' is dropped from the summary and S-16 (attack 2, accepted).
2. MODEL IGNORES OR SELF-RESUMES. Mitigated by the short packet with no resume command, the SKILL.md sentence, the held status line, the grace backstop (state is durable, so the kill is race free) and a released-by-other record that fails `stop`. Evidence of compliance is thin: five short probes on the env route where the models ended their turn, with a packet that printed an owner-only resume command (Claude 5, 8 and 10 turns; Grok 5; Codex 10 [M, re-read]). Nothing covers the recommended packet text, a long run after compaction, or an Improve child in flight. Unknown at scale.
3. CONTRADICTORY TEXT (attack 1, accepted, verified): (a) status_block prints 'The packet prints the resume command' for every paused state; (b) SKILL.md step 5 tells the model to use a paused packet's printed resume command once; (c) the refusal footer says 'do not end the turn over a refused callback'. Fixed by the held branch, one SKILL.md sentence and StopPointHeld; tested through the real gate (I3-1, I3-2, I3-7).
4. PACKET GROWTH. None for active packets: the held branch is unreachable unless held (regression guard I2-8; report 1 measured identical digests of 44 normalised packets). The held packet is 1,139 characters in a long scratch path, against 11,064 to 18,874 for the generic paused packet [M].
5. READ AS AN S-10 CAP. The stage form fires after the stage's loop has ended and never interrupts one; the S-10 sentence says so; test I2-2 shows no stop at a producer result.
6. SAVED RUNS. Optional key, so none are refused; an older ShipLoop refuses a run that carries the key. Accepted under one supported version.
7. ACCIDENTAL ARMING IN A REAL RUN and the S-14 stall hazard (a forgotten armed stop stalls an unattended run). No environment route, no packet advertises the verb, the armed stop is visible in `status` and state.md, `stop-at --clear` removes it, and S-16 says the stop is opt-in.
8. METRIC GAMING (a stopped run looks cheap or passes). `shiploop`, `committed` and `checks` are n/a, never a pass; no baseline row; scope label 'partial: stopped after <stage>'; a grace-killed host reads 'honoured, host ignored the stop' in the verdict and the summary line.
9. HOST DIFFERENCES. The verb route is host-independent. The environment route would fail where Claude's CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB is set [M, report 2].
10. PASSES HERMETIC TESTS, FAILS LIVE. The hermetic suites cannot show the no-relaunch property on a real host (FAKE hosts never run the CLI [M]); the ladder puts one live smoke on a resumable host (Grok) before the long probe, and the Claude smoke is not counted as evidence for no-relaunch because ClaudeHost is not resumable [M].
11. SIDE EFFECTS (corrected from the draft, which said lint keyed on history rows). Item and knowledge commits key on history rows and run after the save [M, _item_commit, _knowledge_close]: unchanged. Lint keys on status [M, lint.on_transition]: fixed by the lint_view line and tested by I4-a. Ordering: the stop is saved before the item and knowledge commits [M, dispatch order], so a reader keyed on state.md alone can see the repository before the commit lands; the harness therefore reads `reached` as final only after the host has exited. A failed knowledge commit at a stop is not retried until the next accepted stage after resume (the existing 'the next accepted stage commits it' behaviour). A crash between save and item commit is the existing window, unchanged.
12. KNOWN LIMITS, DOCUMENTED NOT FIXED: improve-reconcile bypasses the hook (its row has outcome reconcile); pass-level stops are out of reach; a copied stopped run keeps stale absolute paths; a continuation runs on the same plugin install, so it cannot validate a later fix; five test forms collapse to one pause for a not-applicable item.
13. PRE-EXISTING DEFECT, SEPARATE CHANGE: the generic paused packet is cut at PRINT_LIMIT 16,000 and loses its tail, which holds the 'Resume:' line [M: 11,064 characters at intake (report 3), 16,323 after two stages (report 4), 17,672 (report 1), 18,874 in a long scratch path (report 2); re-seen as a 'Full packet:' pointer in lab_paused.out and lensB]. Every user pause can lose its tail. The held packet avoids it by being short. Fixing the generic packet changes printed text for user pauses and belongs in its own change.
14. NEW (real-CLI fake host is new infrastructure) and timing tests are flaky unless arming is deterministic; mitigated by blocking the fake on stop-point.json.
15. NEW: the harness now depends on two hook-status fields. Extra keys are unlikely to break the keepalive reader (it reads named keys [M]) but no exact-key assertion was searched beyond test/shiploop-keepalive.test.py: unknown, the keepalive suite is in the footprint.
16. COST. Engine slice about 150 lines of code with tests of about 400 lines and docs of about 70 [I]; harness about 380 lines with 500 of tests [I]. Dollar and minute savings are not measured; only the planning windows the owner quoted exist (72.7 and 375.0 minutes) and the design does not shorten them, it removes the kill and the lost records.
measurement:
First use proves it in rungs, cheapest first, on the released marketplace version (SPEC: publish, refresh, run). No threshold is invented; each rung is binary on the conditions listed, and numbers are reported as found.

RUNG 0, hermetic (before release): I2 to I6 suites green: the 33-stage grid, the entry-parity matrix, the real Improve import, the real-CLI fake-host runs including no-relaunch.

RUNG 1, tight race, cheapest: `run.py --host claude --case hello --stop-at after:intake`. Prototype probes cost $0.159 and 16.0 s for this stop on the env route [M]; the verb route's cost is unknown. Pass: invocation.json stop_point preflight true; stop-point.json armed rc 0 with seconds and revisions (this records the real arming margin against the 7 to 16 s first-accept window); state.md stop_at.reached set and the last history row intake; host ended by itself; metrics.json, result.json and review-export exist; `stop` passes; no baseline row; termination says stopped at the requested stop point. Then `--stop-at after:research` (prototype: $0.251, 46.3 s, 10 turns [M]) and `shiploop resume` plus `--resume-run` to continue in place.

RUNG 2, resumable host: `--host grok --case hello --stop-at after:intake` (prototype env probe 5 turns, $0.061 [M]). This is the first live proof of the no-relaunch property (Grok and Codex are the hosts that relaunch an ended session [M]). Pass: exactly one session, no relaunch, harness exit 0 on its own. One smoke on Codex for the same stop.

RUNG 3, seeded live Improve-import stop (attack 2, accepted): `--host grok --case battleship --seed-at step-plan --stop-at after:test-spec`, armed synchronously after seed_run with no race. The stages it pays for are step-plan and test-spec through their Improve reviews; on the earlier Grok run those two took 9.4 + 4.5 = 13.9 minutes accept to accept and on Luna xhigh 38.7 + 39.9 = 78.6 [M, stage-clock.md]; the seeded run's own time is unknown.
